subject: Unexpected partial-streaming + stop-token behavior during SeqTech demo prep
messages:
From: Helen Cho <helen.cho@seqtech.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@seqtech.com
Date: 2026-05-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Strange partial output during streaming in our integration

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads-up: while running the integrated demo today our engineers saw the model stream a partial completion and then send a short ']' stop token that ended the stream abruptly. It happened twice in two separate requests to the same Redwood endpoint (same model id & params). The demo relies on streaming incremental JSON and this truncation causes our parser to fail.

We captured a recording and exported the request/response (attached). Can you escalate? We're demoing to our execs next Wednesday and need a reliable workaround.

Details:
- Endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (hosted)
- Model: redwood-open-13b (as shown in console)
- Mode: streaming / chunked-json, content-type application/json-stream
- Behavior: stream stops after a partial token `]` and no finalization event; follow-up request returns normal output

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Cho
Sr. ML Engineer, SeqTech
helen.cho@seqtech.com

Attachments: screencap-truncation.mov (30s), seqtech-repro-20260522.txt (repro steps)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange partial output during streaming in our integration

Thanks for the ping and the repro — I kicked off a quick ingest of the logs. Initial notes: the attached runtime logs show a stream close with an EOF after a partial token in the NVMe buffer; that's unusual. Two quick asks so we can reproduce locally:
1) Exact SDK + version (they mentioned console but not SDK). Is SeqTech using our JS streaming SDK or raw HTTP?
2) Full request headers (especially any intermediate proxy like CloudFront or a customer edge that might alter chunking).

Workaround idea: force `stream: false` or pin to a previous model variant (redwood-open-13b@v1.2) until we confirm. If we can reproduce I can try a kernel rollback to isolate.

I'm opening SUP-9876 and will attach their repro.

- Dev
Dev Patel

dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange partial output during streaming in our integration

Reading the logs now. Quick hypothesis: a recent micro-update to the async chunk flushing in our streaming pipeline (kernel-level change 2026-05-18) attempted to coalesce small token bytes to reduce syscalls; that had one edge-case where a closing stop-token `]` could be emitted as a separate short chunk and an upstream proxy with strict chunk-size/idle-timeout would consider the connection stale and close it, yielding an abrupt EOF.

Triage plan:
- Reproduce using SeqTech's curl in an isolated environment with a simulated proxy (NGINX with chunking/timeouts).
- If reproduced, offer a temporary mitigation: (A) suggest SeqTech set `stream: false` or (B) we rollback the micro-update in the hosted pool for redwood-open-13b@latest for a canary subset and route SeqTech's traffic there until fixed.
- Patch: tighten flush to ensure stop-tokens are emitted appended to the same chunk as final bytes, or add explicit finalization event on streaming channel.

I can have a dev canary by EOD if we prioritize. For the demo ask, we should offer model pin + reduce chunk coalescing on their routed host.

- Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood
logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-24T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: SUP-9876: Root cause & mitigation for SeqTech streaming truncation

Update (SUP-9876): reproduced in staging with NGINX chunking/timeouts; root cause confirmed as the chunk coalescing change from 2026-05-18.

Short-term mitigation we can offer immediately:
- Customer-facing workaround: Pin SeqTech to redwood-open-13b@v1.2 in the console (no code change required) OR set `stream: false` in their integration. Both are safe.
- Platform action: we'll roll a canary rollback for 10% of redwood-open-13b@latest traffic within the hosted pool that includes SeqTech's region; traffic will be routed away from the micro-update. Canary will be monitored for 24 hours.

Risk / brief explanation for leadership: the rollback simply reverts the micro-change that coalesces small writes. It's low risk for model correctness (no model param change) and minimal perf impact (~1-3% additional syscalls under very high tail loads). We will monitor latency/throughput during the canary.

Longer-term fix (in-flight): adjust flush semantics so final stop-tokens are appended, and add an explicit finalization event on the streaming protocol so clients don't rely on connection close. Target: patch + validation in staging within 5 business days.

I'll run the canary tomorrow morning and set the SUP ticket with logs, repros, and the demo rollback timeline. Marissa, I'll draft the customer-facing note and loop in Karthik for approval.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Engineer, Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com
